notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Thursday 26 November; the EGX reopens on Sunday. Wall Street and oil are Friday 27 November closes. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Friday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Thursday's EGX index levels, which no source we opened has published (Amwal Al Ghad's 26 November report is not online), so the index cards show Wednesday's closes and the EGX30 tile uses EnterpriseAM's rounded 0.5% fall; Brent's Friday price, given as $95.44 by Reuters and $90.26 by Investing.com (the chart is flagged); Brent's November fall (nearly 20% per Investing.com, with no Reuters figure); Friday's spot gold price, because the Investing.com article's own figures do not agree with one another; Misr Life's final IPO price, which is due on Saturday and was not published when this edition was prepared.
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Saturday and show Thursday 26 November as the latest session.

items: A drone or missile hits Saudi Aramco's 400,000-barrel-a-day Jazan refinery, killing a worker, as Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites spread → Brent climbs to $96.61, its highest since early November, raising Egypt's fuel import bill.
OPEC+ is likely to keep its output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 at Sunday's meeting, sources tell Reuters → no extra supply keeps oil prices firm.
China's CSI 300 jumps 3.5% on Friday after Beijing pledges more market support; Seoul's Kospi rises 4.1% → a calmer Asia supports emerging-market risk appetite.
The EGX30 falls 0.5% on Thursday as Telecom Egypt drops 2.4%, while Orascom Construction rebounds 3.5% → foreigners are net buyers, but turnover stays 40.9% below average.
Suez Canal revenue doubles to $593 mn so far in November, from $295 mn a year earlier, as major shipping lines return → more dollar income eases pressure on the pound and the current account.
Orascom Construction closes its OCI deal, issuing 97.2 mn new shares, but misses its 24 November listing date → the enlarged company's new shares still await admission to the EGX and ADX.
US core PCE inflation rises to 3.3%, the highest since November 2023, and markets price a December Fed hike at 98% → higher US rates keep pressure on emerging-market flows and the pound.
The EGX30 falls 0.68% to 50,538.66 as local investors sell; the pound weakens to 54.76 per dollar at the CBE → turnover stays thin at EGP 6.2 bn, 43.3% below the 90-day average.

The Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Hodeidah port, and the Houthis threaten all Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah → a wider Red Sea war raises the risk to Suez Canal traffic and Egypt's shipping costs.
The AI sell-off returns: Seoul's Kospi falls 6.16% and Taiwan 4.94% on Wednesday after the Nasdaq drops 1.5% → doubts over AI returns and new US tariff threats weigh on global risk appetite.
The EGX30 edges up 0.34% to 50,885.33 as Sidpec jumps 5.4% → the index is still 10.2% below its 6 September peak.
Retail investors cover only 0.19x of Misr Life's public tranche on day one → the soft start tests demand for the state's biggest listing of the year.
The EGX30 rebounds 1.44% to 50,711.96 on Monday and small caps jump 3.41%, recovering part of Sunday's sell-off → every stock in the 21-stock table except Emaar Misr rises as global markets steady.

Misr Life Insurance opens its IPO book at EGP 12.00 to 13.60 a share, valuing it at EGP 60 to 68 bn → the whole range sits below the EGP 13.82 fair value set by its adviser; trading is due around 3 December.

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang and the Nasdaq jumps 6.5%, its best day since April 2025; Taiwan rises about 9% on Tuesday → the AI trade revives after last week's rout, lifting risk appetite worldwide.
Brent falls 3.46% to $89.37, its lowest close since 31 August, as Libya restarts the Sharara pipeline → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill.

The EGX30 drops 2.85% to 49,989.79 on Sunday and small caps fall 5.55%, as local investors sell after Wall Street's correction → foreigners are the only net buyers; turnover stays 40.4% below its 90-day average.
Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt divert to Europe, and fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas at $12.75/mmBtu → Europe outbids Cairo for scarce cargoes, raising costs for energy-hungry industry.
US stock futures jump 2.2% on Monday after the S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday into a correction → a rebound abroad could steady the EGX after Sunday's sell-off.
Tankers are set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi refinery → Gulf attacks keep oil's risk premium alive; Brent holds near $92.7.

key.l: S&P 500 in the week to 27 Nov

stories.h: Wall Street ends its best week since April 2025 as AI stocks rebound
stories.what: In Friday's shortened session the S&P 500 rises 1.60% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow 1.18% to 50,774.94. For the week the S&P gains 5.6%, its best since April 2025, the Nasdaq 6.68% and the Dow 5.46%, though the S&P and Nasdaq remain on track for their worst November since 2008. Chipmakers lead, with Micron up 7.6%. Futures price a 96.2% chance of a December Fed hike.
stories.why: Bargain hunters return to battered AI and chip stocks.
stories.aff: Global equities and emerging-market risk appetite.
stories.eg: A calmer Wall Street supports flows into Egyptian assets.

key.l: OPEC+ targets set to stay unchanged

stories.h: OPEC+ agrees in principle to hold output targets as Iraq pushes for more
stories.what: OPEC+ reaches an agreement in principle to keep output targets unchanged in the first quarter of 2027 before Sunday's meetings, three sources tell Reuters. Iraq, whose preliminary capacity is 4.9 mn barrels a day, seeks a higher quota. WTI settles 0.7% lower at $83.08 on Friday, while Brent ends the week up about 3%. President Trump backs Iraq's crackdown on oil smuggling, which Baghdad says cost it about $100 bn from 2008 to 2025.
stories.why: Producers disagree over capacity estimates and face a possible surplus next year.
stories.aff: Oil prices and Egypt's fuel import and subsidy bill.
stories.eg: Steady output keeps oil costs high for Egypt.

key.l: ships the US says it has disabled under its Iran blockade

stories.h: US disables another blockade runner; Gulf allies condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
stories.what: The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman, at least the 15th vessel stopped since its Iran blockade began in April; it says it has redirected 158 ships since July. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say a tanker hit a mine in Hormuz. Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye condemn Houthi attacks that have killed at least 26 people in Saudi Arabia since 23 September. Italy says the drone that killed two of its citizens in Kuwait was made in Iran.
stories.why: The US-Iran war and the Saudi-Houthi conflict both target shipping and energy sites.
stories.aff: Gulf shipping, insurance and oil supply.
stories.eg: Shipping risk keeps freight and import costs high for Egypt.
stories.egx: Bearish for shipping and import-heavy sectors.

key.l: Misr Life retail cover on day one

stories.h: Misr Life's institutional book closes; the final price is due Saturday
stories.what: Institutional subscriptions for Misr Life Insurance closed on Friday; the final price is due on Saturday and retail orders close on Monday. Retail investors covered the public tranche 0.19x on day one, ordering about 7.09 mn of 37.5 mn shares, and pay only 25% upfront. Trading should start on or around Thursday 3 December.
stories.why: The state sells part of a large insurer.
stories.aff: IPO demand and the state's divestment plan.
stories.eg: The final price will show how institutions value the insurer.
stories.egx: Neutral until the price is set.

stories.h: EGX30 ends a volatile week with a 0.5% fall on Thursday
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.5% on Thursday on turnover of EGP 6.4 bn, 40.9% below the 90-day average, after a 0.68% fall to 50,538.66 on Wednesday. International investors are the only net buyers on Thursday. Raya Holding (+5.2%), Orascom Construction (+3.5%) and Edita (+2.9%) lead the gainers; Telecom Egypt (-2.4%), Qalaa (-1.8%) and e-finance (-1.6%) lead the losers. The index is up 20.3% this year.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause.
stories.eg: Thin trade before the Misr Life listing and the Fed meeting.
stories.names: Orascom Construction, Edita (up); Telecom Egypt, Qalaa (down).
